## Ask the map first

One command answers each question in a few hundred tokens, from the committed map
and a live index of the working tree. Run it before you search, edit or close a defect.

| Question | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Who owns this file, what tests and cites it, is it one of a class? | `python scripts/project_map.py q <path>` |
| Where else does this defect live? | `python scripts/project_map.py class <path or symbol>` |
| Which tests exercise this file? | `python scripts/project_map.py tests <path>` |
| What else moves when this changes? | `python scripts/project_map.py impact <path>` |
| Where is this function defined and used? | `python scripts/project_map.py q <symbol>` |
| How many places do this, and whose are they? | `python scripts/project_map.py grep <regex>` |
| What does this component do and depend on? | `python scripts/project_map.py q <component id>` |
| Which doc section, component or file covers a topic? | `python scripts/project_map.py q <words>` |
| Who owns this directory? | `python scripts/project_map.py q <directory>/` |
| Every command on one card | `python scripts/project_map.py brief` |

## Classification contract

| Class | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `current` | Supported by present repository or operational evidence. |
| `planned` | Explicitly specified by an authoritative roadmap, plan, or contract. |
| `inferred` | Strongly implied by at least two sources and labelled with confidence. |
| `proposed` | An unresolved choice that must remain visible. |
| `legacy` | Retired historical material with one semantic owner and per-path metadata. |

Implementation, operation, and governance are separate lifecycle axes. An authored
component can therefore be implemented while dormant or still under governance review.

## Sibling sets

Files that share one contract or one copied implementation. A defect or a change
in one member reaches the others, so sweep every member before closing it.
`python scripts/project_map.py class <member>` lists each set with the clones and
namesakes the live index finds. Evidence for every set is in the JSON.

## Material cautions

- `project.boundary`: Keep all credentials in the mylaunchpad vault collection. Do not copy credentials into .env files.
- `project.boundary`: Polar is also used by YieldEngine, but the products have separate credentials and source.
- `project.boundary`: The pylaunchpad Brain scope owns durable external context.
- `quality.tests.app_api-app_billing-app_bootstrap-data_models`: These are source associations. They do not prove runtime test coverage.

## AI consumption guidance

Use `project_map.json` for complete evidence, relationships, path ownership, and
filterable lifecycle data. Treat the `classification` field as the fact and future
boundary. Never promote `planned`, `inferred`, or `proposed` content to current fact.
Treat `nodes[].paths` as associations: exact current files assert an eligible owner,
while wildcards and directories group related material. Resolve unique primary
ownership and read policy through `inventory.manifest`. Node and graph coverage
counts derive from this manifest and do not claim test success. The backwards-compatible
`inventory.path_index` and `nodes[].inventory_count` describe content ownership only.
Legacy retains its semantic stub and has exact metadata records in the manifest.
The Files view pages through every manifest record. The separate local `workspace.html`
adds ignored and untracked names, dependencies, VCS metadata and link boundaries.
Refresh local metadata with `workspace --write`; deterministic checks exclude it.
`catalogues[]` and `entry_points[]` are resolved against the same inventory, so a
path they name is tracked at the recorded source digest.
